question.worked_solution:
For compatible matrices $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ and scalar $\alpha ,$ the Hadamard product has the following properties:

- Commutativity:

$$
A⊙B=B⊙A
$$

- Associativity:

$$
(A⊙B)⊙C=A⊙(B⊙C)
$$

- Distributivity over Addition:

$$
A⊙(B+C)=A⊙B+A⊙C
$$

- Scalar Distributivity:

$$
\alpha (A⊙B)=(\alpha A)⊙B=A⊙(\alpha B)
$$

In this case, by the scalar distributivity of the Hadamard product, we have

$$
(\alpha Y)⊙X+{Z}^{T}=\alpha (Y⊙X)+{Z}^{T}.
$$

Then, by the commutativity of the Hadamard product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\alpha (Y⊙X)+{Z}^{T} & =\alpha (X⊙Y)+{Z}^{T} \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}]+{[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -9 & 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 & 4 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6-5 & -3+4 \\ -9+2 & 12-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
